final_answer:
Let
\[
g(x)=x^5+a x^3+b x^2+x=x\bigl(x^4+a x^2+b x+1\bigr).
\]
The system is
\[
\ddot x+(1+x^2)\dot x+g(x)=0.
\]

Define
\[
F(x)=\int_0^x g(s)\,ds
=\frac{x^6}{6}+\frac{a x^4}{4}+\frac{b x^3}{3}+\frac{x^2}{2},
\]
and
\[
V(x,y)=\frac{y^2}{2}+F(x).
\]
Then
\[
\dot V=y\dot y+g(x)\dot x
=y\bigl(-g(x)-(1+x^2)y\bigr)+g(x)y
=-(1+x^2)y^2\le 0.
\]

So the origin is globally asymptotically stable exactly when it is the only equilibrium. Equilibria satisfy \(y=0\) and
\[
x\bigl(x^4+a x^2+b x+1\bigr)=0.
\]
Thus we need
\[
q(x)=x^4+a x^2+b x+1>0
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R.
\]

For \(r>0\),
\[
q(r)>0 \iff b>-\left(r^3+ar+\frac1r\right),
\]
and
\[
q(-r)>0 \iff b<r^3+ar+\frac1r.
\]
Hence the condition is
\[
|b|<\inf_{r>0}\left(r^3+ar+\frac1r\right).
\]
Let
\[
h(r)=r^3+ar+\frac1r.
\]
Its minimum occurs when
\[
h'(r)=3r^2+a-\frac1{r^2}=0.
\]
Writing \(s=r^2\), this is
\[
3s^2+as-1=0,
\]
so
\[
s=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+12}-a}{6}.
\]
At this point,
\[
\frac1r=3r^3+ar,
\]
so
\[
\min h(r)=4r^3+2ar=2\sqrt{s}(2s+a).
\]
This minimum is positive exactly when \(a>-2\). Therefore the desired condition is
\[
a>-2,\qquad |b|<2\sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{a^2+12}-a}{6}}
\left(a+\frac{\sqrt{a^2+12}-a}{3}\right).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
|b|<\frac{2}{3}\bigl(\sqrt{a^2+12}+2a\bigr)
\sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{a^2+12}-a}{6}}.
\]

Under this condition, \(q(x)>0\), so \(g(x)\) has the sign of \(x\). Hence \(F\) is positive definite and proper, \(V\) has compact sublevel sets, all forward solutions exist globally, and LaSalle’s invariance principle gives convergence to the only invariant set in \(\{\dot V=0\}\), namely \((0,0)\).

If the condition fails, then \(q\) has a real zero or touches zero, giving another equilibrium \((x,0)\ne(0,0)\), so global attraction to the origin is impossible.

\[
\boxed{
\left\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:\ a>-2,\ 
|b|<\frac{2}{3}\bigl(\sqrt{a^2+12}+2a\bigr)
\sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{a^2+12}-a}{6}}
\right\}
}
\]
